title: NY State Assembly · District 54
area: Bushwick and East New York in Brooklyn, including Cypress Hills and City Line.

context.text: Open seat, uncontested in the general election. Christian Celeste Tate (D/WFP) defeated incumbent Erik Dilan 61.9%–37.9% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary (a third candidate, Paperboy Prince, withdrew or was disqualified before the primary). Dilan, in office since 2015, is not on the November ballot. No Republican or other party candidate qualified, so Tate is running unopposed in the general election.

candidates.name: Christian Celeste Tate
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated incumbent Erik Dilan 61.9%–37.9% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary; running unopposed in the general election.

summary.text: Christian Celeste Tate is a community organizer and consultant who describes himself as a democratic socialist. He is First Vice Chair of Brooklyn Community Board 4 and won the Democratic nomination for the open NY State Assembly District 54 seat by defeating incumbent Erik Dilan in the June 2026 primary; he also holds the Working Families Party line and is unopposed in November. According to his campaign, he is running on housing, immigration and public-safety platforms; this is his first run for public office.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he grew up the son of a special education teacher and a small business owner, and his parents sent him and his sister to a private school.

After graduating with degrees in government and economics, he worked as a strategy consultant; his campaign website says that after the 2020 BLM protests in New York he dedicated himself to social change and now works as an impact consultant with philanthropists and nonprofits on poverty and inequality.

Organizes on housing with the East New York Community Land Trust, which his campaign website says includes knocking on doors, organizing rallies and standing with neighbors in court against predatory investors, and is North Brooklyn Chapter Chair of New York Communities for Change.

Served as East Brooklyn Field Coordinator for Zohran Mamdani's mayoral campaign and has led canvasses for Working Families Party candidates, according to his campaign website; City & State also reports he volunteered for the Mamdani campaign.
Is a member of NYC-DSA, where he helped lead the Afrosocialists and Socialists of Color Caucus, and of its North Brooklyn Branch's Community Solidarity Committee, according to his campaign website.

Is First Vice Chair of Brooklyn Community Board 4 and chairs its transportation committee; his campaign website says he helped write the board's 2025 Responsible Development Policy and advocated for accessibility at the Wilson Avenue subway station.

Has not previously held elected office. In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary he defeated incumbent Erik Dilan, 61.9% to 37.9%, per Ballotpedia; City & State reports he knocked on 4,000 doors during the campaign.

Ballotpedia lists endorsements from U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders and NYC-DSA, and City & State reports endorsements from the Democratic Socialists of America, the Working Families Party and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

priorities.text: Housing: create a state Social Housing Development Authority to build permanently affordable homes statewide; support tenant organizing through the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act; expand Good Cause eviction protections; defend rent stabilization; renew the Bushwick/East New York cease-and-desist zone; and tax speculative home flipping.

Immigration: pass "New York for All" to bar state agencies from collaborating with ICE; adopt "Access to Representation" to guarantee immigration lawyers in deportation cases; and pass "Dignity Not Detention" to bar immigration detention facilities from operating in New York.

Public safety: invest in youth programming and workforce development, expand violence interruption programs, and increase access to school counseling, mental healthcare and substance-use treatment, framing these as addressing root causes of crime rather than only responding to it.

positions.summary: Supports creating a state Social Housing Development Authority, passing the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act, expanding Good Cause eviction protections, and defending rent stabilization.
positions.quote: We will support tenant organizing through the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act. We will expand Good Cause protections and defend rent stabilization.

positions.summary: Opposes expanded immigration enforcement; supports barring state agencies from cooperating with ICE, guaranteeing immigration lawyers in deportation cases, and prohibiting immigration detention facilities in New York.
positions.quote: We will pass New York for All to prohibit state agencies from collaborating with ICE.

positions.summary: Frames public safety primarily as a matter of community investment and prevention — youth programming, workforce development, violence interruption, and mental-health and substance-use services — rather than increased police funding or staffing.
positions.quote: Real public safety comes from community investment and prevention. We have to do more than just respond to crime when it happens; we have to address the generational cycles of poverty and inequality that cause crime in the first place.

positions.summary: Lists organizing campaigns to "tax the rich" among his community organizing work and campaign goals.

candidates.researchNotes: Tate has never held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record; background, priorities and positions are drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, the only public campaign-statement source located.
